Having run over all the settled parts, of which I got a tolerable bird's-eye view, I took it into my head that I should like to see something of real backwoodsman's life.

arxiv-1911-03356.title: On Incentive Compatible Role-based Reward Distribution in Algorand Thanks: M. Fooladgar and M. H. Manshaei are equally contributing authors.
arxiv-1911-03356.creator: Mehdi Fooladgar, Mohammad Hossein Manshaei, Murtuza Jadliwala, Mohammad Ashiqur Rahman
arxiv-1911-03356.description: Abstract Algorand is a recent, open-source public or permissionless blockchain system that employs a novel proof-of-stake byzantine consensus protocol to efficiently scale the distributed transaction agreement problem to billions of users. In addition to being more democratic and energy-efficient, compared to popular protocols such as Bitcoin, Algorand also touts a much high transaction throughput.

arxiv-2012-11309.title: Gegenbauer kernel filtration on the unit hypersphere
arxiv-2012-11309.creator: Louis Omenyi, McSylvester Omaba
arxiv-2012-11309.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Louis Omenyi, McSylvester Omaba. Filtration of quantifiable objects by smoothing kernels on Riemannian manifolds for visualisation is an ongoing research. However, using common filters created for linear domains on manifolds with non-Euclidean topologies can yield misleading results. While there is a lot of ongoing research on convolution of quantifiable functions with smoothing kernels on the lower dimensional manifolds, higher-dimensional problems particularly pose a challenge. One important generalization of lower dimensional compact Riemannian manifolds is the unit hypersphere.

arxiv-2209-00693.title: A large dataset of software mentions in the biomedical literature
arxiv-2209-00693.creator: Ana-Maria Istrate, Donghui Li, Dario Taraborelli, Michaela Torkar, Boris Veytsman, Ivana Williams
arxiv-2209-00693.description: Abstract We describe the CZ Software Mentions dataset, a new dataset of software mentions in biomedical papers. Plain-text software mentions are extracted with a trained SciBERT model from several sources: the NIH PubMed Central collection and from papers provided by various publishers to the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.

arxiv-2401-07351.title: On min-base palindromic representations of powers of 2
arxiv-2401-07351.creator: Donald L. Kreher, Douglas R. Stinson
arxiv-2401-07351.description: Abstract A positive integer N N is palindromic in the base b b when N = ∑ i = 0 k c i ​ b i N=\sum_{i=0}^{k}c_{i}b^{i} , c k ≠ 0 c_{k}\neq 0 ,and c i = c k − i , i = 0 , 1 , 2 , … , k c_{i}=c_{k-i},\;i=0,1,2,...

arxiv-2402-05563.title: Neural Multigrid Architectures
arxiv-2402-05563.creator: Vladimir Fanaskov
arxiv-2402-05563.description: Abstract We propose a convenient matrix-free neural architecture for the multigrid method. The architecture is simple enough to be implemented in less than fifty lines of code, yet it encompasses a large number of distinct multigrid solvers. We argue that a fixed neural network without dense layers can not realize an efficient iterative method.

arxiv-2406-00511.title: Clinical utility of automatic treatment planning for proton therapy of head-and-neck cancer patients using JulianA
arxiv-2406-00511.description: Abstract Background: Automatic treatment planning promises many benefits for both research and clinical environments. For research, autoplanning provides the ability to include treatment planning as a part of a reproducible workflow that can be run at the press of a button after changing any parameter, algorithm or model, which is particularly useful for applications in machine learning and artificial intelligence.

arxiv-2410-14201.title: Text-to-Image Representativity Fairness Evaluation Framework
arxiv-2410-14201.creator: Asma Yamani, Malak Baslyman
arxiv-2410-14201.description: Abstract Text-to-Image generative systems are progressing rapidly to be a source of advertisement and media and could soon serve as image searches or artists. However, there is a significant concern about the representativity bias these models embody and how these biases can propagate in the social fabric after finetuning them.

arxiv-2502-03256.title: Matter Creation Cosmologies and Accelerated Expansion
arxiv-2502-03256.creator: Sudip Halder, Jaume de Haro, Supriya Pan, Tapan Saha, Subenoy Chakraborty
arxiv-2502-03256.description: Abstract Non-conservation of dark matter can lead to late-time cosmic acceleration. This mechanism is known as the matter creation theory and this replaces the need of dark energy and modified gravity theories. We consider a two-fluid system consisting of a cold dark matter and a second fluid with constant barotropic equation of state.

arxiv-2502-13709.title: Generically τ \tau -regular irreducible components of module varieties
arxiv-2502-13709.creator: Grzegorz Bobiński, Jan Schröer
arxiv-2502-13709.description: Abstract . In the representation theory of finite-dimensional algebras, the study of projective presentations of maximal rank is closely related to the study of generically τ \tau -regular irreducible components of varieties of modules over such algebras. We show that a module is τ \tau -regular if and only if its minimal projective presentation is of maximal rank.

arxiv-2503-19131.title: Turbulent dynamos in a collapsing cloud
arxiv-2503-19131.creator: Muhammed Irshad P, Pallavi Bhat, Kandaswamy Subramanian, Anvar Shukurov
arxiv-2503-19131.description: Abstract The amplification of magnetic fields is crucial for understanding the observed magnetization of stars and galaxies. Turbulent dynamo is the primary mechanism responsible for that but the understanding of its action in a collapsing environment is still rudimentary and relies on limited numerical experiments.

arxiv-2512-17904.creator: Stéphane Bessy, Daniel Gonçalves, Amadeus Reinald, Dimitrios M. Thilikos
arxiv-2512-17904.description: Abstract We investigate the problem of strong connectivity augmentation within plane oriented graphs. We show that deciding whether a plane oriented graph D D can be augmented with (any number of) arcs X X such that D + X D+X is strongly connected, but still plane and oriented, is NP -hard.

pmc-11312716.title: Molecular Modification Enhances Xylose Uptake by the Sugar Transporter KM_SUT5 of Kluyveromyces marxianus
pmc-11312716.creator: Xiuyuan Luo, Xi Tao, Guangyao Ran, Yuanzhen Deng, Huanyuan Wang, Liyan Tan, Zongwen Pang
pmc-11312716.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This research cloned and expressed the sugar transporter gene KM_SUT5 from Kluyveromyces marxianus GX-UN120, which displayed remarkable sugar transportation capabilities, including pentose sugars. To investigate the impact of point mutations on xylose transport capacity, we selected four sites, predicted the suitable amino acid sites by molecular docking, and altered their codons to construct the corresponding mutants, Q74D, Y195K, S460H, and Q464F, respectively. Furthermore, we conducted site-directed truncation on six sites of KM_SUT5p.

pmc-11474241.title: Understanding visual perception in visual snow syndrome: a battery of psychophysical tests plus the 30-day clinical diary
pmc-11474241.creator: Simona Garobbio, Reza Mazloum, Michael Rosio, Jeanette Popovova, Raphaela Schöpfer, Fabienne C Fierz, Leah R Disse, Konrad Peter Weber, Christoph J Schankin, Lars Michels, Michael H Herzog
pmc-11474241.description: Patients with visual snow syndrome (VSS) experience uncountable flickering tiny dots in the entire visual field. Symptoms often persist over the years. Very little is known about altered perception in VSS. VSS is diagnosed based on subjective reports because there is no manual with objective measures.

pmc-12382062.title: The association of bone mineral density with cardiovascular disease and mortality among individuals with/without type 2 diabetes: a population-based retrospective cohort
pmc-12382062.creator: Ran Chen, Qingshan Guo, Chuanqing Bai, Jie Li, Yiyang Chen, Jiaxin Tan, Lianyang Zhang, Jun Fei, Siru Zhou
pmc-12382062.description: ObjectivesWhile type 2 diabetes (T2D) disrupts bone metabolism, T2D individuals often exhibit normal or elevated bone mineral density (BMD), complicating the relationship between BMD and cardiovascular disease (CVD). This study aimed to clarify the associations of BMD with CVD and mortality (CVM) in individuals with/without T2D.Study designa retrospective cohort study.

pmc-12489211.title: Quadriceps Tendon Rupture in Young Female Patient with Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Long-Term Hemodialysis: A Case Report
pmc-12489211.creator: Ghuna Utoyo, Adrian Ismiarto, Renata Junilla
pmc-12489211.description: Objectives:Chronic kidney Disease (CKD) describes the gradual loss of kidney function. Some studies have shown that patients with CKD also have a reduction in muscle quality, which translates into low muscle strength or physical performance per unit of muscle mass or volume. This concept of low muscle quality is closely associated with muscle fat infiltration (MFI).

pmc-12708617.title: Evaluation of Lens culinaris germplasm against ascochyta blight by applying phenotyping and defense genes attributes
pmc-12708617.creator: Mohsen Modareskia, Hamid Hatami Maleki, Behrouz Shiran, Hamid Reza Pouralibaba
pmc-12708617.description: Lentil Ascochyta blight (caused by Ascochyta lentis) is one of the most important limiting factors of lentil cultivation and production in most regions of the world. Introducing resistance sources against the pathogen is a suitable strategy to conquer this biotic stress. In this study, A. lentis-lentil pathosystem was inspected through the evaluation of 79 lentil genotypes in greenhouse conditions.

pmc-12826366.title: Prevalence & utilisation of AI chatbots for medical education among students of medical colleges
pmc-12826366.creator: Aditya B. Saran, Shivkumar R. Kolle, Dheeraj Maheshwari, Sarah Al Hinnawi, Aryash L. Dhoke, Meghana M. Date, Aditi B. Saran
pmc-12826366.description: cenarios, receive simplified explanations, and summarise difficult topics. A national study from China showed that although only 28.72 per cent of students actively used ChatGPT, most recognised its potential to improve efficiency and understanding in students’ learning1. Similarly, a study from the USA highlighted ChatGPT’s popularity for aiding clinical reasoning and exam preparation2.

pmc-12974818.title: Two’s company, three’s a crowd: Social situations alter group dynamics in the maritime earwig (Anisolabis maritima)
pmc-12974818.creator: Michael Nolan-Tamariz, Vikram K. Iyengar
pmc-12974818.description: Sexual selection can lead to dimorphic traits that can affect an individual’s behavior including how individuals respond to different social situations. We examined how sex and body size influence aggression and courtship in different-sized groups of the maritime earwig, Anisolabis maritima (Order Dermaptera), an insect in which males and females differ morphologically and behaviorally.

pmc-13207210.title: Education and Provision of a Pest Management Tool Kit to Residents in Low-Income Housing: Effect on Cockroach Reduction
pmc-13207210.creator: Xiaodan Pan, Souvic Sarker, Jin-Jia Yu, Richard Cooper, Changlu Wang
pmc-13207210.description: Simple SummaryGerman cockroaches are the most common pest in low-income housing across the U.S. Many residents are unaware of effective ways to control them. This study tested whether educating residents about integrated pest management (IPM) and providing cockroach control products could help reduce cockroach infestations.

pmc-13258535.title: Fungal β-1,3-glucans: Cell Wall Constituents That Promote Gut Health Through Innate Immune Modulation
pmc-13258535.creator: Fnu Samiksha, Drishtant Singh, Sudi Shatha Harbool, Luca Di Martino, Caroline Kruithoff, Thomas S. McCormick, Mahmoud Ghannoum
pmc-13258535.description: Fungal β-1,3-glucans are structurally conserved polysaccharide components of the fungal cell wall that exhibit potent immunomodulatory activity. These molecules are recognized by pattern recognition receptors, Toll-like receptors, complement receptor 3, lactosylceramide, scavenger receptors, and EphA2. Binding of β-1,3-glucans through these receptors triggers coordinated innate and adaptive immune responses such as cytokine production, phagocytosis, and trained immunity.

pmc-13547606.title: Celestial neuromorphics based on ferroelectric gallium oxide
pmc-13547606.creator: Ke Xu, Zhannan Guan, Mengjiao Pei, Yurong Luo, Yonghao Zhu, Xinxin Yu, Lin Hao, Songhao Gu, Jiahao Yao, Zhanhua Li, Xinyi Pei, Yuhao Zhang, Han Wang, Changjin Wan, Qing Wan, Rong Zhang, Jiandong Ye
pmc-13547606.description: Efficient recognition of celestial activities demands hardware that can operate with high efficiency and robustness in radiation-rich space environments. Ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) semiconductors are well-suited for such environments, but conventional UWBG transistors are not inherently compatible with advanced computing functions.

pmc-13558835.title: METTL3 Promotes Lipid Deposition and Pulmonary Fibrosis by Destabilizing PLIN2 in a m6A‐Dependent Manner
pmc-13558835.creator: Qiping Liu, Rui Xu, Xianzhi Du
pmc-13558835.description: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a lethal lung disorder that is associated with aberrant lipid metabolism. N6‐methyladenosine (m6A) methylation is involved in IPF progression. However, whether METTL3, a m6A methyltransferase, modulates lipid metabolism in IPF remains unknown. In this study, we aimed to investigate the effects of METTL3 on fibrosis and lipid accumulation and identify the molecular mechanism.

pmc-13574972.title: The influence of college students’ AI literacy on perceived usefulness: a moderated mediation model with AI anxiety and trust across disciplinary backgrounds
pmc-13574972.creator: Zihan Li, Jiaying Han, Liwei Wu, Xiaogang Wang
pmc-13574972.description: BackgroundTo investigate how AI literacy influences perceived usefulness among university students from different disciplinary backgrounds, this study examines the roles of AI anxiety and trust.MethodsBased on 563 valid samples collected from university students, a moderated mediation model was utilized to explore AI anxiety as a mediator and trust as a moderator across various disciplinary backgrounds.

pmc-13669755.title: Post–endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography pancreatitis prophylaxis: a stratified assessment for evaluation of risk approach
pmc-13669755.creator: David S. Braun, Prashant S. Kedia, Mingyang Cui, Paul R. Tarnasky
pmc-13669755.description: Background and AimsThe risk of post–endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) pancreatitis (PEP) is influenced by patient and procedure-related factors. Strategies to decrease PEP are of great importance. This study aimed to determine if PEP prophylaxis (PEPX) could be avoided in patients in whom high-risk procedure-related factors are avoided as guided by a Stratified Assessment for Evaluation of Risk (SAFER) approach.
